explanation:
Baseline feedback records status "success" with training MSE 0.02516 / NMSE 0.15339; no runtime error, type mismatch, or shape problem was observed. Therefore no repair of an observed failure is warranted, and the task contract (signature, finite (len(u0),) output, 0-16 valid params) must be preserved exactly.

The only actionable change is a structural refinement within the same declared parameter count of 15: the previous hypothesis used a single three-way cubic monomial (p10*u0*u1*u2), which is a narrow single basis direction, plus a duplicative saturating/damping pair. I replace the cubic monomial with the squared summed pair-products cross term, giving one extra distinct quadratic-in-interaction direction while keeping the count at 15, and re-target the second saturating term onto the u0*u2 product so it is not collinear with the u1 saturation term.

This is a hypothesis about basis richness only; it is not a claim of improved NMSE, which depends on the host's bounded least-squares fit from ones under the frozen allocation. All inputs remain read-only one-dimensional arrays, np is the only dependency, no file/network/subprocess access and no row-index or label encoding is used.
